compactRecord.rs: Japan's most pristine wilderness; the only UNESCO Natural Heritage site in Hokkaidō, where bears walk to the shore beneath sea-cliff waterfalls.
compactRecord.td: UNESCO World Heritage primeval peninsula (registered 2005) at Hokkaido's NE tip, famed for brown bears, Steller's sea eagles and pack drift ice. Reached via Rte 334 to Utoro; sightseeing cruises from Utoro & Rausu ports.

compactRecord.rs: Most iconic Shiretoko viewpoint — lakes mirror the entire Shiretoko ridgeline; elevated boardwalk lets visitors enter bear country safely.
compactRecord.td: Five small lakes reflecting the Shiretoko volcanic range, in primeval forest above Utoro. An 800 m elevated boardwalk (closed Nov-late Apr) offers bear-safe access; ground trails open May-Jul require guides during brown-bear peak.

compactRecord.rs: One of Japan's only river-bathing waterfalls — wade up a warm volcanic stream in primeval wilderness above the Sea of Okhotsk.
compactRecord.td: Hot-spring waterfall on the Kamuiwakka River inside Shiretoko NP — the entire creek is naturally heated by Mt Iōzan above. Reached only by shuttle bus from Utoro in summer; visitors wade the warm cascade upstream.

compactRecord.rs: Rare cliff-side waterfall fed by groundwater, not a river — emerges straight from a 100 m sea-cliff above the Okhotsk.
compactRecord.td: 'Maiden's Tears' — a 100 m cliff waterfall on the Sea of Okhotsk shore where groundwater seeps out of the Shiretoko Plateau and drops directly into the sea. A 20 min trail from the Shiretoko Nature Center near Utoro.

compactRecord.rs: Japan's most inaccessible cape — no roads, no trails; reached only by sea, with brown bears routinely seen from the boat.
compactRecord.td: Roadless northern tip of the Shiretoko Peninsula, accessible only by sightseeing cruise from Utoro or Rausu. Towering basalt cliffs, hanging waterfalls, brown bears on the shore. The boundary of the UNESCO core zone.
